correctness.rationale: For \(u=k\cosh(ax/\sigma^2)\ge k\), direct differentiation gives exactly \(\sigma^2(\log f)''(x)=-1+b(u+k^2)/(1+u)^2\). The rational derivative has one explicitly located maximizer, with the center/interior bifurcation at \(k=1/2\). Two disjoint monotonic root parametrizations prove a single sharp threshold, and principal Lambert branches are fixed by their argument ranges. An elementary sign-controlled entire power series proves the unimodal, non-log-concave witness; orthogonal factorization proves the multivariate form. All dimension and endpoint quantifiers are analytic, not inferred from finite tests. The packaged standalone checker reports 283 passed assertions and is auxiliary.

originality.rationale: The literature establishes general posterior-covariance Hessian identities and sharp bounds on the number of Gaussian-mixture modes. Those are not claimed original. The compared papers and targeted mathematical-record searches did not supply the sharp two-parameter global Hessian maximum, the exact Lambert boundary, or a certified unique-mode/non-log-concave witness together. No external independent scholarly assessment of correctness or priority has occurred.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete continuous two-parameter shape classification of a basic symmetric three-component Gaussian mixture, not a single numerical slice. Optimal log curvature is quantitatively needed to determine global log concavity and best strong-concavity modulus; modal upper bounds alone do not answer either question. An explicit unique-mode/non-log-concave example demonstrates a substantive boundary between commonly interchanged hypotheses. Results do not purport to classify arbitrary three-Gaussian mixtures.
